facts.fact: The minister urged organisations not yet registered with the Data Protection Commission to register, and said the Commission must be central to protecting data in the new SIM registration, treating it as a working body.
The minister called for compliance with the Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843), which he treated as the law in force, while a new Data Protection Bill is being developed.
The minister said organisations should register with the Data Protection Commission, which he said must be central to the SIM registration's data protection.
The minister said the government has launched the One Million Coders Programme to equip young Ghanaians with skills in coding, AI, data protection and digital engineering; no trained count is given.

facts.fact: The minister said the Ghana Card is the key unique identifier for all Ghanaians today and the single source of truth for identity verification.
The minister said the Ghana Card is used for identity verification when opening a bank account online or applying for government healthcare.
The minister named banking and government healthcare as services verifying identity against the Ghana Card.
The minister said Cabinet decided to begin a new SIM card registration with live verification against the National Identification Authority database.
